title: Leaves not generated by the simulation
body:
Good morning everyone, 

I am currently using CPlantBox to develop the architecture of the Arabidopsis Thaliana. 

To do so, I need to be able to set leaves as successor of all the stems. Though it is possible with the main stem (by setting a leaf organ and a stem organ with the same subType and then only change the _la_ default value of the stem by 0), it is not possible with secondary stems (i.e. stems successor of the main stem). 

More precisely, the code run without problem, but no leaves are created on the secondary stems. 

There is the important part of the code used :
[buggy_leaves.zip](https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/files/5094341/buggy_leaves.zip)

And there is a commented picture of the result :
![leaves_not_appaering](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44650226/90598477-67067380-e1f3-11ea-93a9-de95a471cfaf.png)

I hope this problem is explained well enough.

Thank you in advance for the help.

title: New Visualisation pipeline to both VTK and Unreal
body:
A bit late with this, but here's a short summary of my work. I will refer to below at different points.

### New Vis Module

I have added a CMakeLists and a PlantVisualiser class in the visualisation section of CPlantBox. PlantVisualiser requires a MappedPlant as I use functions that are present in MappedPlant, as well as the leaf geometry that is also provided already in the leaf classes. Based on that, I make a full geometrization of the plant that is continuous organ-wise.

![plant_trans](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9272590/236769319-d68b601e-543d-40f5-8c9e-fe08d74381d8.png)

In the future, I will do a bit more work on the junctions of the visualization to round it up a bit more.

The simple setup is also shown in the example:

https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/blob/6bb3875960a18b6f06a8c070d4ad03bf03f6c953/tutorial/examples/example_vis.py#L50-L55

**There is vis ambiguity**

As I start with a coordinate system at the beginning of the plant, I am setting a certain way the leaf blade connects to its parent organ. From there, I am following a 1D line in space, which is generally not a problem, but the leaf blade shape and behavior in space requires more parametrization potentially. I am heavily punishing the z component of the right vector (which locally points in y direction). This should be iterated upon in the future.

**Windows changes**

There is still some work to be done here, I already talked to @m-giraud about this. There are some peculiarities of the MSVC compiler that I addressed. We are likely halfway to building it on Windows.

### Code Details

https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/blob/6bb3875960a18b6f06a8c070d4ad03bf03f6c953/src/CMakeLists.txt#L14-L15

I amended this because the build folder might not be the same as the root folder. We could do this for the rest of the dependencies too eventually.

https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/blob/6bb3875960a18b6f06a8c070d4ad03bf03f6c953/src/PyPlantBox.cpp#L195-L227

I also included a python binding for the quaternions, but I will also reiterate over that specific implementation as well as it is sometimes possible that the no-scaling property of the quaternion is not always respected in operations, and I added auxiliary normalizations in code.

https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/blob/6bb3875960a18b6f06a8c070d4ad03bf03f6c953/src/visualisation/PlantVisualiser.h#L62-L68

The comment style mainly assisted my coding process and we can change or reverse anything here.

title: WIP: Modify build system to allow generation of wheels and Debian packages
body:
Hi,

or internal use we wanted to distribute CPlantBox either via Python wheels or using Debian packages, and I could not find any information on that in the code.  Therefore, I thought our changes might be interesting to other users of CPlantBox. However,  feel free to close the PR or suggest relevant changes in case you want to keep (some) of these changes.

In order to generate the packages, some changes to the build system were required - I'm not completely sure if these changes have any unintended side effects for other general use cases of CPlantBox (i.e., I had to revert the target location of the .so files back to their default).

Anyway, the current state allows the generation of wheels and Debian packages, as tested on a Debian bookworm and an old Debian 10.13 (Buster) installation. Please also note that wheels could directly be uploaded to pypi.org, enabling to install CPlantBox easily via an `pip install cplantbox` for supported architectures/interpreters.

## Build instructions

Starting in a clean virtualenv:

`pip install build wheel ninja`

I had some problems with the pybind11 version, but 2.4 and 2.11.1 finally worked:
```
cd src/external/
rm -rf pybind11
# for older systems (i.e. Debian 10.13)
git clone --depth 1 -b v2.4 https://github.com/pybind/pybind11.git
# Debian Bookworm worked with:
git clone --depth 1 -b v2.11.1 https://github.com/pybind/pybind11.git
```

Wheels are then built with:

`python setup.py bdist_wheel`
or
`python -m build --wheel`


## Debian packaging

```
# on Debian ookworm
pip install stdeb
# for Debian Buster:
pip install stdeb==0.9.1
pip install setuptools==40.8.0

```

The Debian packages are then generated using:

`python3 setup.py --command-packages=stdeb.command bdist_deb`

output is located in **deb_dist/**

title: Number of laterals (leaves) depends on timestep size
body:
Hi, 

When running a script to simulate lettuce plants (same as my previous issue), I noticed that the number of laterals seems to depend on timestep size which looks like a bug more than a feature ?

Here is a table that recaps the number of leaves at the final timestep (tf = 30 days). All other parameters are left equal, only the timestep size changes. The expected number of leaves is computed as: (lmax-la-lb)/ln + 1 (per the CRootBox paper, Schnepf et al. 2018) and is approx. 12.6.

| dt [d] | Number of leaves |
| ---- | ---- |
| 10 | 13 |
| 5 | 12 |
| 1 | 11 |
| 0.1 | 10 |
| 0.01 | 10 |
| 0.001 | 10 |

My understanding is that a smaller timestep could interact with the dx and dxMin parameters of the main stem and thus have an impact on the emergence of laterals ?

Edit to add the parameter file and associated script
[lactuca_num_leaves.zip](https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/files/14282190/lactuca_num_leaves.zip)

title: Master4 trai rhizo
body:
update CPlantBox to make it work with TriaRhizo (==> add soil exudation).
The 'core files' changed are:

- src/functional/XylemFlux.h: added a function to make kr depend on the distance from the root tip. When the carbon-limited growth is implemented, we cannot use the age-dependent kr variation
- src/functional/XylemFlux.cpp:  
        [a] replaced kr_f with kr_f_wrapped. Now if a leaf segment is belowground (resp. leaf segment below ground), we have kr = 0 instead of a computational error
[b] sumSegFluxes() and splitSoilFluxes(() adapted for full plants 

- src/structural/MappedOrganism.cpp:
[a] setRectangularGrid(), MappedPlant::simulate(): if we have a growing root system and a dumux-cpb coupling, we can set noChanges==True, so that segments remain in the voxel there were first aloccated to.
[b] MappedPlant::calcExchangeZoneCoefs(): compute the distance from the tip of each root segment, used afterwards by the xylemflux class when computing kr

title: build(python): add Linux and macOS wheel artifacts [run-test]
body:
This PR adds CI-built Python wheel artifacts for CPlantBox (relevant issue: https://github.com/Plant-Root-Soil-Interactions-Modelling/CPlantBox/issues/216)

- Adds `pyproject.toml` packaging via `scikit-build-core==0.12.2` and `cibuildwheel==3.4.1`.
- Builds GitHub Actions wheel artifacts for:
  - Linux x86_64 manylinux: `cp311`, `cp312`, `cp313`, `cp314`
  - macOS native architecture: `cp311`, `cp312`, `cp313`, `cp314`
- Fixes Python extension linkage so `plantbox` links as a Python extension module and does **not** embed/link `libpython`.
- Packages installed model data so wheel installs work outside the source tree.
- Builds pinned SuiteSparse/SUNDIALS dependencies from source for wheel builds; system native deps remain explicit opt-in.
- Adds installed-wheel smoke testing plus Linux/macOS wheel audits for portability issues such as `libpython`, host paths, RPATH/install-name leaks, and unexpected dynamic SuiteSparse/SUNDIALS deps.
- Keeps the CMake split for readability:
  - `cmake/CPlantBoxPiafMunch.cmake`
  - `cmake/CPlantBoxPython.cmake`
- Adds concise wheel/native dependency docs and a helper to download latest successful wheel artifacts:
  - `scripts/download-latest-wheel-artifacts.sh`

## Intentionally out of scope

- No PyPI/TestPyPI publishing.
- No Linux aarch64, macOS universal2, or Windows wheels.
- Existing native `cmake . && make install` path is preserved, while packaging/provider options are added for wheel builds.


Here is an example run from my fork showing the resulting artifacts: https://github.com/georgiansarghi/CPlantBox/actions/runs/26345035364

title: Add Windows AMD64 wheel builds (run-wheels)
body:
Adds Windows AMD64 wheels (cp311 to cp314) to the wheel builds from #312, toward the remaining half of #216.

## What this does

* Builds the same pinned native dependencies (SUNDIALS 4.0.2, sha-verified tarball; SuiteSparse 5.3.0, pinned commit) as static MSVC libraries. SuiteSparse 5.x only ships Makefiles, so a small committed CMake project reproduces the Makefile variant matrix (int/long and real/complex compilations of the same sources) through generated stub files.
* Makes the C++ build MSVC-compatible. The whole codebase needed only one source change: two lambdas in `Perirhizal.cpp` captured `[*this]` and used `this->` inside, which MSVC rejects; they now capture the one needed double. The rest is CMake: guarding the GCC-style flags, accepting `.lib` archives in the source-provider checks, and `WINDOWS_EXPORT_ALL_SYMBOLS` on the DLL (the sources have no dllexport declarations, so MSVC otherwise produces no import library).
* Adds a `windows-latest` job mirroring the Linux and macOS ones: cibuildwheel, delvewheel repair, per-python artifacts, and the same `run-wheels` opt-in gating.

## Verification

Full matrix run on my fork (all three platforms, all four pythons, every wheel pip-installed with the `fipy,vis` extras and passing `scripts/wheel/smoke_test.py` on its own platform):
https://github.com/musharna/CPlantBox/actions/runs/33453840741

The Windows smoke test reports the same simulation result as Linux (25 organs, 15 nodes, 14 segments).

## Notes for review

* `--ignore-existing` for delvewheel: the wheel already ships `CPlantBox.dll` next to the extension module, the same layout the Linux/macOS wheels use, and CPython loads extension modules with `LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_DLL_LOAD_DIR`, so same-directory dependencies resolve; the smoke test exercises exactly this.
* `PYTHONUTF8=1` on the build step works around a delvewheel bug (RECORD rewritten in the locale encoding, which corrupts the accented `modelparameter/*Pagès*.xml` filenames on Windows). I will report that upstream to delvewheel separately.
* Both plain (`klu.lib`) and lib-prefixed (`libklu.lib`) copies of the SuiteSparse libraries are installed because SUNDIALS 4.0.2's `FindKLU` drops the empty prefix when it prepends `lib` to `CMAKE_FIND_LIBRARY_PREFIXES`, so it can only find lib-prefixed names on Windows.
* The PyPI-publishing half of #216 is intentionally not included; that needs a project decision about the PyPI account and trusted publishing, and I would be glad to help with it as a follow-up.

title: Make virtualenv Python selection robust in CPlantBox CMake (fix Windows wheel build)
body:
The "Build Windows AMD64 wheels" job failed at CMake configure with `Could NOT find Python3 … Cannot run the interpreter …/venv/bin/python3`. The configure step forced `Python3_EXECUTABLE` to `$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin/python3`, but Windows venvs put the interpreter at `Scripts/python.exe`.

The failing run (`9d9146d`) still had the unconditional `bin/python3` path. The tree already had a `WIN32` branch for this. This PR hardens it.

- **`cmake/CPlantBoxPython.cmake`**
  - The `$VIRTUAL_ENV` override now applies only if `Python3_EXECUTABLE` isn't already set. A value from scikit-build-core or the user is no longer clobbered.
  - It picks `Scripts/python.exe` on Windows and `bin/python3` elsewhere, and applies the override only if that file exists. If it's missing, `find_package(Python3)` does its normal discovery instead of failing on a bogus path.

```cmake
if(NOT Python3_EXECUTABLE AND DEFINED ENV{VIRTUAL_ENV})
    if(WIN32)
        set(_cpb_venv_python "$ENV{VIRTUAL_ENV}/Scripts/python.exe")
    else()
        set(_cpb_venv_python "$ENV{VIRTUAL_ENV}/bin/python3")
    endif()
    if(EXISTS "${_cpb_venv_python}")
        set(Python3_EXECUTABLE "${_cpb_venv_python}")
    endif()
endif()
```

I haven't run the Windows wheel job against this change. Please re-run the `Wheels` workflow to confirm.
